definition: Unique match identifier used to group events and prevent train-test leakage across the same match.
role_in_analysis: Grouping key for model splitting, OOF prediction, and match-level summaries.
notes: If match_id is unavailable, a composite match key should be constructed from teams, date, season, and competition.

definition: Identifier of the possession sequence to which an event belongs.
role_in_analysis: Used to keep continuation-value windows within the same possession sequence.
notes: Sliding windows for receiver continuation value should not cross possession or match boundaries.

definition: Team in possession or team performing the pass, depending on the source table convention.
role_in_analysis: Used for descriptive and case-study summaries; optional in xPass modeling depending on generalisability assumptions.
notes: Including team identifiers in xPass may improve prediction but can reduce interpretability as a pure pass-difficulty model.

definition: Player who performed the pass.
role_in_analysis: Used to estimate passer marginal contribution from out-of-fold residuals.
notes: Player-level estimates should be shrunk toward zero to reduce instability for low-volume players.

definition: Match minute of the passing event.
role_in_analysis: Used as a temporal feature and for event ordering.
notes: Should be numeric and combined with second for chronological sorting.

definition: Second within the match minute of the passing event.
role_in_analysis: Used as a temporal feature and for event ordering.
notes: Should be numeric and combined with minute for chronological sorting.

definition: Start location of the pass in StatsBomb coordinate format.
role_in_analysis: Parsed into start x and y coordinates for xPass features and spatial value calculation.
notes: Coordinates should be checked and, if necessary, transformed so that attacking direction is consistently left to right.

definition: End location of the pass in StatsBomb coordinate format.
role_in_analysis: Parsed into end x and y coordinates for pass geometry and spatial value calculation.
notes: Missing end locations should be excluded or handled consistently before modeling.

definition: Raw pass start x-coordinate.
role_in_analysis: Intermediate coordinate used to compute normalized start location and pass geometry.
notes: StatsBomb pitch length is commonly treated as 120 units.

definition: Raw pass start y-coordinate.
role_in_analysis: Intermediate coordinate used to compute normalized start location and pass geometry.
notes: StatsBomb pitch width is commonly treated as 80 units.

definition: Raw pass end x-coordinate.
role_in_analysis: Intermediate coordinate used to compute normalized end location and pass geometry.
notes: Used with sx to calculate pass length and progression.

definition: Raw pass end y-coordinate.
role_in_analysis: Intermediate coordinate used to compute normalized end location and pass geometry.
notes: Used with sy to calculate pass angle and lateral movement.

definition: Normalized pass start x-coordinate on a 0 to 1 scale.
role_in_analysis: Input to the spatial value function and continuation-value model.
notes: Calculated as sx divided by pitch length.

definition: Normalized pass start y-coordinate on a 0 to 1 scale.
role_in_analysis: Input to the spatial value function and continuation-value model.
notes: Calculated as sy divided by pitch width.

definition: Normalized pass end x-coordinate on a 0 to 1 scale.
role_in_analysis: Input to the spatial value function and continuation-value model.
notes: Calculated as ex divided by pitch length.

definition: Normalized pass end y-coordinate on a 0 to 1 scale.
role_in_analysis: Input to the spatial value function and continuation-value model.
notes: Calculated as ey divided by pitch width.

definition: Pass outcome indicator, where 1 denotes a completed pass and 0 denotes an incomplete pass.
role_in_analysis: Target variable for xPass training and residual calculation.
notes: For StatsBomb event data, pass_outcome is typically missing for completed passes.

definition: Euclidean pass length calculated from start and end coordinates.
role_in_analysis: Core pass-geometry feature for xPass and turnover proxy estimation.
notes: May differ slightly from provider-supplied pass_length if coordinate parsing or orientation differs.

definition: Absolute pass angle, usually calculated from the arctangent of vertical and horizontal displacement.
role_in_analysis: Used to represent pass direction difficulty and turnover-location uncertainty.
notes: Should be consistently calculated after coordinate orientation.

definition: Indicator of whether the passer was under defensive pressure at the time of the pass.
role_in_analysis: Used in xPass prediction, stratified analysis, and turnover proxy estimation.
notes: Derived from the under_pressure field when available.

definition: Forward component of pass displacement or pass length multiplied by cosine of pass angle, depending on script context.
role_in_analysis: Used as a compact directional feature in xPass and continuation-value modeling.
notes: Positive values generally indicate forward progression when coordinates are oriented left to right.

definition: Indicator for whether the event occurred before minute 45.
role_in_analysis: Temporal feature used to capture coarse match-period differences.
notes: Can be replaced by more detailed time-period indicators if needed.

definition: Estimated probability that the pass will be completed given its context.
role_in_analysis: Defines pass success probability and is used to compute risk and expected reward.
notes: For the analytical sample, this should preferably be an out-of-fold prediction grouped by match.

definition: Out-of-fold xPass probability predicted for events held out at match level.
role_in_analysis: Recommended probability input for risk-reward calculation and passer residual estimation.
notes: Prevents the downstream framework from relying on in-sample predictions.

definition: Calibrated xPass probability from the final fitted xPass model.
role_in_analysis: Useful for model deployment or prediction on future data.
notes: If computed on the same training sample, it should not replace OOF xPass for residual-based analyses.

definition: Failure probability of the pass, calculated as 1 minus xpass_prob.
role_in_analysis: Main risk dimension in the risk-reward framework.
notes: Values are usually clipped away from exactly 0 and 1 for numerical stability.

definition: Spatial value of the pass start location based on the EPV-like spatial value proxy.
role_in_analysis: Used to calculate direct spatial progression gain.
notes: This is a location-based proxy, not a full tracking-data EPV model.

definition: Spatial value of the pass end location based on the EPV-like spatial value proxy.
role_in_analysis: Used to calculate direct spatial progression gain.
notes: The difference EPV_end minus EPV_start represents immediate spatial gain.

definition: Opponent-oriented spatial value at the mirrored pass start location.
role_in_analysis: Auxiliary component of failure-cost estimation.
notes: Used to stabilize the cost estimate rather than treating the turnover point as the only consequence.

definition: Opponent-oriented spatial value at the mirrored pass end location.
role_in_analysis: Auxiliary component of failure-cost estimation.
notes: Represents the potential danger if possession is lost close to the intended destination.

definition: Observed continuation-value label for successful passes, computed from short-horizon future value changes within the same possession.
role_in_analysis: Training target for receiver continuation-value modeling.
notes: Defined only for successful passes to avoid mixing possession termination with post-success continuation quality.

definition: Predicted continuation value conditional on pass completion.
role_in_analysis: Included in GainOnSuccess as a short-horizon contribution beyond immediate spatial gain.
notes: Estimated from within-possession event sequences and treated as conditional on success.

definition: Shrunken player-level residual contribution based on success minus xPass probability.
role_in_analysis: Modest adjustment term for individual passer ability in GainOnSuccess.
notes: Should be estimated out of fold and shrunk toward zero to reduce in-sample and low-volume bias.

definition: Estimated normalized x-coordinate of the proxy turnover point along the pass trajectory.
role_in_analysis: Used to calculate the main opponent spatial value component of CostOnFailure.
notes: This is a heuristic proxy because event data usually do not contain the exact interception point.

definition: Estimated normalized y-coordinate of the proxy turnover point along the pass trajectory.
role_in_analysis: Used to calculate the main opponent spatial value component of CostOnFailure.
notes: Should be interpreted as a proxy rather than an observed defensive action location.

definition: Opponent-oriented spatial value at the estimated turnover proxy point.
role_in_analysis: Primary component of CostOnFailure.
notes: Given greater weight than start and end opponent values in the baseline specification.

definition: Conditional gain if the pass is completed, combining immediate spatial gain, receiver continuation value, and passer marginal contribution.
role_in_analysis: Reward component of the expected reward equation.
notes: Baseline form: direct spatial gain + lambda_cv × receiver_CV_cond + passer_weight × passer_marginal.

definition: Estimated spatial cost if the pass fails, based primarily on the opponent value at the turnover proxy point.
role_in_analysis: Failure-cost component of the expected reward equation.
notes: Baseline form: 0.70 × EPV_opp_turnover + 0.15 × EPV_opp_start + 0.15 × EPV_opp_end.

definition: Ex ante expected net reward of the pass.
role_in_analysis: Main outcome variable of the risk-reward framework.
notes: Baseline form: xpass_prob × GainOnSuccess - (1 - xpass_prob) × CostOnFailure.

definition: Expected reward divided by risk.
role_in_analysis: Auxiliary ratio used to describe reward efficiency relative to failure exposure.
notes: Should be interpreted cautiously for very low-risk passes because the denominator is small.
